sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 31-01-2024.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 31-01-2024 at about 3.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-EA-5173 near Palace main gate, Palace road, Bengaluru city within the jurisdiction of High Grounds Traffic Police Station, Bengaluru city, at that time, the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.

entities.text: High Grounds Traffic Police Station, Bengaluru city
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to nearby Hospital,
wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter shifted to Manipal hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Consultant at Doyensys Consulting Service Co. Ltd. and was getting salary of Rs.60,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is unable to do his normal work as before to the accident and sustained permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.2-owner has not appeared before the court,
hence, he has been placed exparte.
After service of notices, respondent No.1-insurer has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

Respondent No.1 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, at the time of accident, the insured vehicle had no valid and effective permit as on the date of accident so also the police have chargesheeted under Sec.56 r/w 192(a) of MV Act.
It has contended that petitioner was riding the scooter who has not having driving license hence, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Water Tanker bearing Reg.
No.KA-43-1122 by its driver, in RTA took place on 31.01.2024 at about 3.30 p.m. near Palace main gate, Palace road, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Petitioner has also examined MRD of Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as PW2 and through him got marked one document at Ex.P12.

Per contra the respondent No.1-insurance company examined its official as RW1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R.1 and R.2.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
8. ISSUE NO.1 : That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of-examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, PW.1 produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1 - FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner.
The contents of Ex.P.1 & 2 are in consonance with the petition averments.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P2, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch of the accident spot was prepared by the IO.

On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 & 4 mahazar and rough sketch it is found that the driver of the offending water tank bearing No.KA-43-1122 changed his lane towards the right side and caused the accident.
This once again evidentiates that the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 by changing his lane dashed against the rare side of the motor cycle of the petitioner.
In the Ex.P.5 IMV report the offending Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 has got scratches in its front right side.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P3 & 4 mahazar and rough sketch along with the contents of Ex.P5 IMV report supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligence driving by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122.

sentences.text: Ex.P9 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the offending Water Tanker bearing No.KA- 43-1122 wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA- 43-1122 .
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence on the part of petitioner.

11. The respondent No.1 - insurer has filed written statement by denying the negligence and its liability and also the official of respondent No.1 -insurance company examined himself as RW1 deposed that he has no personal knowledge about the accident and he has given evidence on the basis of police documents.
12. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 .
13.
The charge sheet is came to be filed against the driver of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122.

entities.text:
2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 .

15. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.

There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/
4 absence of rebuttal evidence.

entities.text: Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 31-01-2024 which is caused by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 which belonging to respondent No.2.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.2.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

19. The petitioner has produced Discharge summaries at Ex.P8 which shows that the petitioner sustained dorsal foot defect with tendon, bone exposure- post traumatic left foot with multiple abrasions both lower limb took treatment as inpatient at Manipal Hospital from 31-01-2024 to 10-02-2024, from 27-02- 2024 to 28-02-2024 and at Apollo Spectra Hospital from 15-08-2024 to 16-08-2024.
The Ex.P8 discloses that the petitioner was nearly hospitalized for totally 15 days.
20. The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him at the time of accident.
Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries.

21. According to the petitioner he was working as Consultant at Doyensys Consulting Services Co.
Ltd., Chennai and getting salary of Rs.60,000/- p.m.

entities.text:
Doyensys Consulting Services Co.
Ltd., Chennai
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: To prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

22. While determining the compensation this court has to looked into the pain and sufferings,
medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.6 & 8 - wound certificate and discharge summaries, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injuries.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.60,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills which are marked as Ex.P-9 amounting to Rs.1,17,143/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
The PW1 in his cross-examination has admitted that in the inpatient bill some amount is paid by the medical insurance.

In this regard on perusal of the medical bills produced at Ex.P9 total Rs.1,17,143/- is claiming by the Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/
5 petitioner.

entities.text: Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Amongst the said bill Sl. No.23, 24 is inpatient bill.
In Sl. No.23 the total inpatient bill was Rs.4,34,478/- out of which Rs.3,94,045/- is paid by the Vidal Health Insurance and Rs.40,433/- is paid by the petitioner.
The petitioner also furnished the advance receipts to show the payments made by him.

Further the Sl.
No.34
the total inpatient bill was Rs.1,90,532/- out of which Rs.1,42,818/- was paid by the Vidal Health Insurance and Rs.33,020/- was paid by the petitioner.
In the evidence affidavit filed by the petitioner also he is claiming only the amount paid by him and not the amount paid by the health insurance.

Hence, the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the said medical bills of Rs.1,17,143/- by rounding off the same to Rs.1,17,200/-
(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed above makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries as per Ex.P8 which shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and also admitted to the hospital on three times.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.
But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability.
At the time of cross-examination also the PW.1 admitted that at that he has continued with his earlier job in the same company.

Further in the judgment reported in 2020(4) KCCR 2621 between Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & another wherein it is held that no compensation could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not effect claimant's capacity to work.

entities.text: Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These answers given by the PW.1 evidentiates that the petitioner is continued in the service and no disability is caused which effects his earning capacity.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

6 (E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period.

entities.text: Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, no evidence are placed in this regard.
In spite of sufficient time the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he has got loss of pay and loss of leave.
Hence, in the absence of any evidence, petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
F) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained simple and grievous injuries in the accident.
As per Ex.P8 the petitioner has spent 15 days in the hospital as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards attendant charges.
(G) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Admittedly the petitioner is continued with his earlier job.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following Towards pain and sufferings - Rs. 60,000/- Towards Medical expenses - Rs. 1,17,200/-
 Towards diet, food, - Rs. 40,000/-
 nourishment, attendant and  conveyance charges  Towards loss of future earning - NIL  capacity  Loss of income during laid up - NIL  period  Towards attendant charges - Rs. 15,000/-
 Towards loss of amenities - Rs.
 Total - Rs. 2,62,200/-
23.
Liability:-
The respondent No.1 is the insurer of the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.
24. The respondent No.1 examined its official as RW.1 by contending that at the time of accident the the insured offending vehicle was not having fitness certificate.

In this regard the respondent No.1 insurance company relied on the Ex.P.7 charge sheet wherein at the time of investigation itself the Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/
7 IO has found that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-43-1122 was not having fitness certificate.

entities.text: Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contents of Ex.P.7 is not denied by the petitioners in this regard.
Thereby it is established before this tribunal that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was not having valid fitness certificate.

25. The respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid fitness certificate to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

26. The respondent No.1 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of fitness certificate to the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-43-1122 and also proved the same on the basis of contents of Ex.P.7.
The evidence as per Ex.P7 charge sheet clearly set out the aspect regarding non existence of the fitness certificate to the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-43-1122 at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 is placed exparte and has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of fitness certificate to the offending vehicle.
27. By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 was covered with insurance.
But at the time of accident there was no valid fitness certificate to the offending vehicle.
28. The learned counsel for the petitioner relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.7439/2013 between Rajesh Poojary, V/s Rajesh & others held as follows:

" 9. The Division Bench of this Court in a decision rendered in MFA No.6621/2006 c/w MFA.CROB No.304/2006 in the case of the 'New India Assurance Co. Ltd. -vs- Sri N Srinivasa Murthy and others' (DD 18.9.2007) has observed that 'absence of fitness certificate cannot be a reason to deny the compensation to the claimant'.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. -vs- Sri N Srinivasa Murthy and others' (DD 18.9.2007
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of the Branch Manager -vs- H D Channadevaiah and others in MFA No.4428/2013 c/w MFA No.3553/2013 (DD 25.6.2014) held in a similar circumstances, where the insured vehicle did not possess fitness certificate as on the date of accident that, "the policy was in force on the date of accident and the Insurance Company cannot disown its liability."

entities.text: Branch Manager -vs- H D Channadevaiah and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.1512/2013 between Ramanna V/s K.H. Devaraja & others wherein it is held as follows:
"18. This Court in the similar facts and circumstances in the other case also held that absence of valid FC is not a fundamental breach, in view of Section56 of MV Act and the same has been considered and discussed in detail in the Division Bench judgment of this court in the appeal in MFA No.5993/2015 dated 22.12.2020.
Hence, I do not find any force in the contention of the counsel appearing for the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal has committed an error in exonerating the liability of Insurance Company.

Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/
8 19.

entities.text: Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The other contention of the learned counsel for the respondent No.3- Insurance Company is that it is a case of pay and recovery.

The said aspect is considered by the Division Bench of this Court and this Court has categorically held hat the Insurance Company cannot disown its liability only on the ground that there is no valid FC, it is also his contention that at the time of issuance of policy, the vehicle was having FC and the same was expired on 21.01.2011.
it is unfortunate that the accident has taken place on 30.01.2011 within 10 days of the expiry of the FC.

When the Insurance Company has issued the policy covering the risk for the period from 20.03.2010 to 19.03.2021 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident the FC had expired cannot be accepted, in view of Division Bench judgment of this Court.
The learned counsel for the insurance company also does not dispute the fact that as on the date of the accident the policy was in force.
Hence, I do not find any force in the contention of the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the insurance company.

Accordingly, I answer Point No.(ii) as 'affirmative', in coming to the conclusion that the Tribunal has committed an error in exonerating the liability of the Insurance Company."
29.
In this case, by relying on the above precedent the insurance company cannot be disowned in its liability only on the ground that there is no valid fitness certificate.
As per the Ex.R.2 as on the date of accident the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.1 company.
Not having the valid fitness certificate is not a fundamental breach of contract and as per Ex.P5 IMV report the accident was not due to any mechanical defect.

Hence, the judgment relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner is aptly applicable to the present case on hand and by relying on the judgment quoted above the insurance company i.e., respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
30.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,62,200/- (Rupees Two lakhs sixty two thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
15. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/
4 absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 31-01-2024 which is caused by the driver of Water Tanker bearing No.KA-43-1122 which belonging to respondent No.2.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability.
Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/
6 (E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period.
Thereby it is established before this tribunal that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was not having valid fitness certificate.
25. The respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid fitness certificate to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
The evidence as per Ex.P7 charge sheet clearly set out the aspect regarding non existence of the fitness certificate to the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-43-1122 at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 is placed exparte and has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of fitness certificate to the offending vehicle.
But at the time of accident there was no valid fitness certificate to the offending vehicle.
Mohammed Irfan vs Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137888220/

In this case, by relying on the above precedent the insurance company cannot be disowned in its liability only on the ground that there is no valid fitness certificate.
As per the Ex.R.2 as on the date of accident the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.1 company.
Not having the valid fitness certificate is not a fundamental breach of contract and as per Ex.P5 IMV report the accident was not due to any mechanical defect.

ISSUE NO.3:
30.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,62,200/- (Rupees Two lakhs sixty two thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
